title: The Sunday Read: ‘What I Found on the 365-Mile Trail of a Lost Folk Hero’

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后有什么。

sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 他们可能几乎每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续助您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com斜杠subscribe上的特惠。

sentences.en: My name is Sam Anderson.
sentences.zh: 我叫萨姆·安德森。

sentences.en: I am a staff writer for the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》杂志的专栏作家。

sentences.en: I kind of write about everything.
sentences.zh: 我几乎什么都写。

sentences.en: I think my beat is subjects that I get totally obsessed with and then force my editors to let me write about.
sentences.zh: 我想我的报道领域是那些让我完全着迷，然后逼着编辑让我写的主题。

sentences.en: And a subject I've been obsessed with for so many years now is the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 而有一个主题让我着迷了这么多年，那就是老皮革人。

sentences.en: He's a sort of legendary folk hero from the 19th century who used to walk in this giant circle, 365 miles around through New York and Connecticut, over and over and over again
sentences.zh: 他是19世纪某种传奇的民间英雄，过去常常在纽约和康涅狄格州之间走一个365英里的大圈，一遍又一遍地走下去

sentences.en: for decades at such regular intervals that people said you could set your clocks by it.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他的间隔如此规律，以至于人们说你可以根据他来对时钟。

sentences.en: He wore this big, funky leather suit that he stitched together himself.
sentences.zh: 他穿着这套由自己缝制的大大的、古怪的皮衣。

sentences.en: And no one knew where he came from or why he was doing this.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道他来自哪里，也不知道他为什么要这样做。

sentences.en: He was a total mystery to the people who lived along his route.
sentences.zh: 对于沿途居住的人们来说，他完全是个谜。

sentences.en: Newspapers published basically like fan fiction about the old Leatherman, origin stories that people just made up about him.
sentences.zh: 报纸基本上发表了关于老皮革人的同人小说，人们只是凭空捏造关于他的起源故事。

sentences.en: I think he was kind of a perfect vehicle for people to express their own anxieties and fantasies
sentences.zh: 我觉得他某种程度上是人们表达自己焦虑和幻想的完美载体

sentences.en: Just all kinds of trauma, tragedy, people projected onto this mysterious guy.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的创伤、悲剧，人们都投射在这个神秘的家伙身上。

sentences.en: I stumbled across the old leather man while I was researching something else.
sentences.zh: 我在研究别的东西时偶然遇到了老皮革人。

sentences.en: And for whatever reason, it hit me like a bolt of lightning.
sentences.zh: 不管出于什么原因，它就像一道闪电击中了我的心。

sentences.en: I think what got to me was, number one, it's a great mystery.
sentences.zh: 我想打动我的是，第一，这是一个巨大的谜团。

sentences.en: But number two, there was something really moving about this man and his relationship to the towns that he walked through.
sentences.zh: 但第二，这个男人以及他与他走过的城镇之间的关系，有一种非常动人的东西。

sentences.en: There was such a generosity from people and genuine curiosity and empathy for him that I found really touching.
sentences.zh: 人们表现出的慷慨、真正的求知欲以及对他的同理心，让我觉得非常感人。

sentences.en: and i think i really related to this guy as strange as it sounds like a lot of people i think i feel sometimes alienated and strange or like i want to drop out of society and here
sentences.zh: 而且我想我真的能和这家伙产生共鸣，听起来很奇怪，我想很多人有时会感到疏离和怪异，或者觉得自己想脱离社会，而这里

sentences.en: was someone who had done it in a totally fascinating way so i would always fantasize about following in
sentences.zh: 正是一个以完全令人着迷的方式做到这一点的人，所以我总是幻想追随

sentences.en: his footsteps sometimes my wife asks me what are you thinking about and i hesitate to answer because it's just the old Leatherman.
sentences.zh: 他的脚步，有时我妻子问我在想什么，我却犹豫着不敢回答，因为脑子里只有老皮革人。

sentences.en: Years passed, and at one point an editor asked me, do you have any weird stories that you've never been allowed to write for the magazine?
sentences.zh: 岁月流逝，有一次一个编辑问我，你有没有什么从不被允许为杂志写的古怪故事？

sentences.en: So for this week's Sunday read, I was able to fulfill my destiny and finally go walking in the footsteps of the old Leatherman on his loop.
sentences.zh: 所以为了本周的周日阅读，我得以实现命中注定的使命，终于踏上了老皮革人的循环路线，追随他的足迹。

sentences.en: I loaded up my backpack, and I just, for many, many, many days, just walked.
sentences.zh: 我背上行囊，就这样，在许许多多的日子里，一直在走。

sentences.en: And I wrote all about it.
sentences.zh: 我把这一切都写了下来。

sentences.en: So here's my story.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事。

sentences.en: Our audio producer today is Adrian HurSt.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的音频制作人是阿德里安·赫斯特。

sentences.en: The original music you'll hear was written and performed by Aaron Esposito.
sentences.zh: 你将听到的原创音乐由亚伦·埃斯波西托创作并演奏。

sentences.en: Sometime in the 1850s or 60s, at a terrible moment in U.S.
sentences.zh: 大约在19世纪50年代或60年代，在美利坚历史上一段可怕的时期，

sentences.en: history, a strange man seemed to sprout out of nowhere into the rocky landscape between New York City and Hartford.
sentences.zh: 一个奇怪的男人似乎凭空出现在纽约市和哈特福德之间的岩石地带。

sentences.en: The word strange hardly captures his strangeness.
sentences.zh: “奇怪”这个词根本无法形容他的怪异。

sentences.en: He was rough and hairy, and he wandered around on back roads, sleeping in caves.
sentences.zh: 他粗鲁而多毛，在乡间小路上游荡，睡在山洞里。

sentences.en: Above all, he refused to explain himself.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他拒绝解释自己。

sentences.en: As one newspaper put it, he is a mystery and a very greasy and ill-odored one.
sentences.zh: 正如一家报纸所说，他是一个谜，而且是一个非常油腻、气味难闻的谜。

sentences.en: Other papers referred to him as the animal, or just throwing up their hands, this uncouth and unkempt what-is-it.
sentences.zh: 其他报纸称他为“动物”，或者索性双手一摊，称这个粗野、不修边幅的“这是个什么东西”。

sentences.en: But the strangest thing about the stranger was his suit.
sentences.zh: 但这个陌生人最奇怪的地方在于他的衣服。

sentences.en: In summer and in winter, in every possible kind of weather, the man wore, from head to toe, an outrageous outfit he seems to have made himself.
sentences.zh: 无论夏天还是冬天，在任何可能的天气里，这个男人从头到脚都穿着一套他自己似乎亲手制作的离谱行头。

sentences.en: Rough leather patches stitched together with long leather strips, like a quilt.
sentences.zh: 粗糙的皮革补丁用长皮革条缝合在一起，就像一条百衲被。

sentences.en: It was stiff, awkward, stinky, and brutally heavy.
sentences.zh: 它又硬又笨拙，发着恶臭，而且重得要命。

sentences.en: It looked like knight's armor, made out of baseball gloves.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像用棒球手套做成的骑士盔甲。

sentences.en: To anyone encountering him on a quiet country lane, he must have seemed almost unreal.
sentences.zh: 对于在安静的乡间小路上偶遇他的人来说，他一定显得很不真实。

sentences.en: A huge slab of brown, twice as wide as a normal man, his suit creaking and squeaking with every step.
sentences.zh: 一大块棕色的东西，比正常人宽两倍，他的衣服每走一步都吱吱作响。

sentences.en: In the years following the Civil War, the wandering stranger became an object of curiosity, then a frequent subject of the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 在内战之后的几年里，这个流浪的陌生人成了一个好奇的对象，随后成了报纸的常客。

sentences.en: People gave him a name, the Old Leatherman.
sentences.zh: 人们给他起了一个名字——老皮革人。

sentences.en: I suppose that many of the readers of your valuable paper have heard of the Old Leatherman, wrote someone from Rye, New York, in 1870.
sentences.zh: 1870年，一位来自纽约莱伊的人写道：“我想你们这份宝贵报纸的许多读者都听说过老皮革人。”

sentences.en: Hearing the reports about this singular recluse, I, in company with others, paid his haunts a visit.
sentences.zh: “在听到关于这位奇特隐士的报道后，我和其他人一起去他的出没地拜访了。”

sentences.en: The Old Leatherman was a sort of real-life Northeastern Sasquatch.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人就像是现实生活中的东北大脚怪。

sentences.en: Curious citizens went plunging into the woods to investigate.
sentences.zh: 好奇的市民冲进树林去一探究竟。

sentences.en: What they found surprised them.
sentences.zh: 他们发现的东西让他们大吃一惊。

sentences.en: The Old Leatherman's caves were orderly, complete with primitive fireplaces, sleeping areas, and stores of food, meat and hickory nuts.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人的山洞井井有条，里面有原始的壁炉、休息区以及储存的食物、肉类和山核桃。

sentences.en: Under one slab of rock, he had dug out an apple cellar.
sentences.zh: 在一块岩石板下，他挖了一个苹果地窖。

sentences.en: In some forests, he kept well-tended gardens.
sentences.zh: 在某些森林里，他保留着精心照料的花园。

sentences.en: month after month people watched the old leather man clomp past their farms and through their woods
sentences.zh: 日复一日，人们看着老皮革人从他们的农场旁、树林中踩着沉重的步伐走过

sentences.en: and right up the main streets of their tiny towns at mealtimes he would stop at sympathetic
sentences.zh: 直接走到他们小镇的主街上，每到饭菜时分，他就会停在那些有同情心的人家门口

sentences.en: households the same ones over and over to ask with a grunt for food he rarely spoke and when he did his words were clipped, strange.
sentences.zh: 总是同一群人，哼着声要求食物，他很少说话，开口时也总是言简意赅、十分怪异。

sentences.en: In the silence, rumors grew.
sentences.zh: 在沉默中，谣言四起。

sentences.en: People speculated that the old leather man was French, or French-Canadian, or Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 人们猜测老皮革人是法国人，或是法裔加拿大人，或者是葡萄牙人。

sentences.en: They said that he couldn't speak at all, or that he just couldn't speak English, or that he spoke English perfectly but pretended not to.
sentences.zh: 他们说他根本不会说话，或者他只是不会说英语，或者他英语说得极好却假装不会。

sentences.en: They said he came from a family in Hartford named Brown.
sentences.zh: 他们说他来自哈特福德一个叫布朗的家庭。

sentences.en: They said he was immune to rattlesnake bites.
sentences.zh: 他们说他对响尾蛇咬伤免疫。

sentences.en: The more he walked, the more fascinated people became.
sentences.zh: 他走得越多，人们就越着迷。

sentences.en: Year after year, the old leather man was like a song stuck in the whole region's head.
sentences.zh: 年复一年，老皮革人就像一首在整个地区人们脑海中挥之不去的歌。

sentences.en: As residents compared notes, as newspaper coverage snowballed, some actual facts became clear.
sentences.zh: 随着居民们互相交流情况，随着报纸的报道呈滚雪球般增加，一些事实开始明朗起来。

sentences.en: For one thing, it turned out that the old leather man was traveling great distances.
sentences.zh: 首先，事实证明老皮革人正在进行长途跋涉。

sentences.en: His network of caves spanned at least 100 miles.
sentences.zh: 他的洞穴网络跨度至少有100英里。

sentences.en: Also, his wanderings weren't random.
sentences.zh: 而且，他的漫游并不是随意的。

sentences.en: They were regular and repetitive.
sentences.zh: 它们是有规律且重复的。

sentences.en: In an effort to map his route, people set up sting operations in the woods.
sentences.zh: 为了绘制他的路线图，人们在树林里设下了伏击网。

sentences.en: They tailed him from town to town.
sentences.zh: 他们从一个镇子尾随他到另一个镇子。

sentences.en: Finally, in the mid-1880s, people realized something astonishing.
sentences.zh: 最终，在19世纪80年代中期，人们意识到了一件惊人的事情。

sentences.en: The old Leatherman was walking in a giant loop, roughly 365 miles around.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人正在走一个巨大环路，全长大约365英里。

sentences.en: It stretched from the Hudson River in the west to the Connecticut River in the east, from mountains in the north to beaches in the south.
sentences.zh: 它西起哈德逊河，东至康涅狄格州河，北到群山，南至海滩。

sentences.en: Along the way, it passed through something like 50 towns.
sentences.zh: 沿途，它穿过了大约50个城镇。

sentences.en: One full circuit usually took him 34 days.
sentences.zh: 完整的一圈通常需要他34天。

sentences.en: His coming can be calculated with almost as much certainty as that of an eclipse, one newspaper wrote.
sentences.zh: 一家报纸写道：“他的到来可以像日食一样以几乎同等的确定性被计算出来。”

sentences.en: Another said,
sentences.zh: 另一家写道：

sentences.en: So regular are his habits that it is often said that he is the only sure thing that farmers can depend upon in this age of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: “他的习惯是如此规律，以至于人们常说，在这个充满不确定性的时代，他是农民们唯一可以确信依靠的事物。”

sentences.en: Soon, the old leatherman became a full-blown media phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 很快，老皮革人成了一个名副其实的媒体现象。

sentences.en: The Hartford Globe published a front-page article complete with a timetable of his travels.
sentences.zh: 《哈特福德环球报》发表了一篇头版文章，并附有他行程的时间表。

sentences.en: In small towns, people lined the streets to watch him pass.
sentences.zh: 在小镇里，人们排在街道两旁看他走过。

sentences.en: Schoolteachers let their students out of class to give him treats.
sentences.zh: 学校老师让学生们下课出来送他零食。

sentences.en: A shop offered promotional old Leatherman postcards.
sentences.zh: 一家商店推出了老皮革人的宣传明信片。

sentences.en: Artists produced woodcuts and paintings.
sentences.zh: 艺术家们创作了木版画和绘画。

sentences.en: Photographers hid cameras in doorways or behind hanging laundry to capture his image.
sentences.zh: 摄影师将相机藏在门廊里或晾晒的衣物后以捕捉他的身影。

sentences.en: The old Leatherman never sought the attention.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人从未寻求过这种关注。

sentences.en: If anything, he avoided it.
sentences.zh: 如果要说的话，他是在刻意避开。

sentences.en: He went out of his way to skirt the region's big cities, Hartford, Bridgeport, New Haven.
sentences.zh: 他绕远路避开该地区的大城市，如哈特福德、布里奇波特、纽黑文。

sentences.en: and if a homeowner got too inquisitive, he would walk away and never come back.
sentences.zh: 如果某个房主表现得过于好奇，他就会走开，再也不回来。

sentences.en: Once in Woodbury, Connecticut, someone presented the old leatherman with some recent articles about him.
sentences.zh: 有一次在康涅狄格州的伍德伯里，有人向老皮革人展示了一些关于他的最新文章。

sentences.en: He grunted over them, the newspaper account read, but showed no enthusiasm at finding himself famous.
sentences.zh: 报纸报道称，他对着这些文章哼了一声，但对于自己出名并没有表现出任何热情。

sentences.en: Who was he?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: Why was he doing this?
sentences.zh: 他为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: People were obsessed, but try as they might, no one could figure it out.
sentences.zh: 人们为之着迷，但无论如何尝试，谁也弄不明白。

sentences.en: One of the most noted philologists in the state spoke to him in a half dozen different languages, the New York Times reported in 1884.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》1884年报道称：“州里最著名的语言学家之一曾用半打不同的语言与他交谈。”

sentences.en: He could get no reply but a guttural sound which meant nothing and which was more animal than human in its character.
sentences.zh: “他得到的只有一种毫无意义的喉音回答，这种声音与其说是人类的，不如说是动物的。”

sentences.en: In the absence of real information, people were happy to invent things.
sentences.zh: 在缺乏真实信息的情况下，人们乐于编造。

sentences.en: Theories emerged.
sentences.zh: 各种理论随之出现。

sentences.en: The old leather man, one man claimed, was disguising himself to evade police.
sentences.zh: 有人声称，老皮革人是为了躲避警察而伪装自己。

sentences.en: He was, quote, a fugitive from justice and a Negro.
sentences.zh: 他“引号：是一个逃犯，而且是个黑人”。

sentences.en: Or he was a wealthy businessman brought low by a fire, mourning the death of his fiancée.
sentences.zh: 或者他是一个被一场大火搞垮的富商，正在哀悼未婚妻的死。

sentences.en: In the end, one origin story conquered all the reSt.
sentences.zh: 最终，一个起源故事战胜了所有其他的传说。

sentences.en: It appeared in 1884 in the Waterbury Daily American under the headline, The Mystery Solved.
sentences.zh: 它于1884年发表在《沃特伯里每日美利坚报》上，标题是《谜团解开》。

sentences.en: Although it was fiction, it spread so far, so fast, that it came to be accepted as truth.
sentences.zh: 虽然那是虚构的，但它传播得如此之广、之快，以至于被当作了真相来接受。

sentences.en: In this version, the old leather man was a Frenchman named Jules Bourglet.
sentences.zh: 在这个版本中，老皮革人是一个名叫朱尔斯·布尔莱的法国人。

sentences.en: As a young man, he fell in love with the daughter of a wealthy leather merchant.
sentences.zh: 年轻时，他爱上了一位富裕皮革商的女儿。

sentences.en: But the merchant disapproved of the match, and so he issued a teSt.
sentences.zh: 但商人不赞成这门亲事，于是他提出了一个考验。

sentences.en: Jules could marry his daughter only if he joined the company, and over the course of one year, proved himself.
sentences.zh: 只有当朱尔斯加入公司并在一年内证明自己时，他才能娶他的女儿。

sentences.en: Things went great until, near the end, Jules made a big investment right before the market crashed.
sentences.zh: 一切都很顺利，直到接近尾声时，朱尔斯在市场崩溃前夕做了一笔大投资。

sentences.en: The company was ruined.
sentences.zh: 公司破产了。

sentences.en: The marriage was forbidden.
sentences.zh: 婚事被禁止了。

sentences.en: And Jules, driven mad by grief, moved to America, where he stitched himself this suit of leather scraps and walked alone in circles for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 而朱尔斯因悲伤过度而发疯，搬到了美洲，在那里他为自己缝制了这套皮革碎片的衣服，并在余生中独自一人在圈子里行走。

sentences.en: It was a real potboiler, a simmering stew of classic 19th century anxieties, class, economic bubbles, madness, immigration.
sentences.zh: 这是一个地道的通俗剧，是19世纪经典焦虑、阶级、经济泡沫、疯狂和移民的一锅慢炖汤。

sentences.en: And yet, people believed it.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们却相信了。

sentences.en: Eventually, the name Jules Bourglet would appear on the Old Leatherman's gravestone.
sentences.zh: 最终，“朱尔斯·布尔莱”这个名字将出现在老皮革人的墓碑上。

sentences.en: In the meantime, year after year, namelessly trailing this ever-expanding cloud of stories, the Old Leatherman continued to walk.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，年复一年，老皮革人无名无姓地拖着这团不断扩大的故事之云，继续前行。

sentences.en: Today, the Old Leatherman is one of those stories that you either really deeply know or have never heard of at all.
sentences.zh: 今天，老皮革人是那种你要么深有了解、要么从未听说过的故事之一。

sentences.en: I discovered it by accident 14 years ago.
sentences.zh: 14年前，我偶然发现了它。

sentences.en: I was having a perfectly normal day, minding my own business, reading a book about local caves,
sentences.zh: 我正过着极其正常的一天，安分守己地读着一本关于当地洞穴的书，

sentences.en: when suddenly this absolute molten chunk of American lore leaped out of the pages and installed himself in my brain.
sentences.zh: 突然，这块绝对融化的美国民间传说熔岩从书页中跃出，驻扎进了我的大脑。

sentences.en: The old leather man hit me with an almost religious force.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人以一种近乎宗教般的力量击中了我的心。

sentences.en: He was a perfect little parable about something both universal and, to me, very personal.
sentences.zh: 他是一个完美的寓言，关于某种既具有普遍性、对我又非常个人的东西。

sentences.en: The tension between alienation and belonging.
sentences.zh: 疏离与归属感之间的张力。

sentences.en: Rejection and rejecting.
sentences.zh: 拒绝与被拒绝。

sentences.en: Who gets to belong to a group?
sentences.zh: 谁有资格属于一个群体？

sentences.en: What are the smallest possible triggers for inclusion or exclusion?
sentences.zh: 接纳或排斥的最小触发因素是什么？

sentences.en: And what happens when someone flips that dynamic?
sentences.zh: 当有人颠倒这种动态时会发生什么？

sentences.en: When the individual is the one rejecting the group?
sentences.zh: 当个人是那个拒绝群体的人时？

sentences.en: Rejecting, in fact, the whole society, but also refusing to go away.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他拒绝了整个社会，但也拒绝离开。

sentences.en: To the people in my life, friends, family, editors, my infatuation with the old leather man quickly became a running joke.
sentences.zh: 对于我生活中的人——朋友、家人、编辑，我对老皮革人的痴迷很快成了一个不断被调侃的笑话。

sentences.en: More than once, my wife has banned me from discussing him in our house.
sentences.zh: 不止一次，我妻子禁止我在家里讨论他。

sentences.en: I've had out-of-body experiences where I've watched myself droning on, unable to stop, making acquaintances late for trains.
sentences.zh: 我有过灵魂出窍的体验，看着自己喋喋不休、无法停下，让熟人们误了火车。

sentences.en: But what was I supposed to do?
sentences.zh: 但我能怎么办呢？

sentences.en: He struck me as a perfect existentialist hero, someone who spurned the false comforts of society, who stood, by choice, out in the cold, harsh wind of reality,
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是一个完美的无神论存在主义英雄，一个唾弃社会虚假舒适的人，他出于选择，站在现实寒冷刺骨的风中，

sentences.en: taking it full blast in the face.
sentences.zh: 正面承受着这一切的冲击。

sentences.en: The old Leatherman was like Melville's Bartleby the Scrivener, except that he refused to even say, I would prefer not to.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人就像梅尔维尔笔下的抄写员巴特比，只不过他甚至拒绝说出“我宁愿不”。

sentences.en: This guy, I thought, had it all figured out.
sentences.zh: 我想，这家伙把一切都琢磨透了。

sentences.en: He managed to remain a part of things while holding himself apart.
sentences.zh: 他设法既置身事外，又融入其中。

sentences.en: In my private fantasy of myself, I was a spiritual descendant of the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 在我对自己内心的幻想中，我是那个老皮匠的精神传人。

sentences.en: I, too, felt alienated from society.
sentences.zh: 我也曾感到与社会格格不入。

sentences.en: The world annoyed me, enraged me, in 10 million different ways.
sentences.zh: 这个世界以千万种不同的方式让我厌烦、让我愤怒，在19世纪时如此。

sentences.en: I spent my childhood pinging between Oregon and California, between apartments and houses, between step-parents.
sentences.zh: 我的童年总是在俄勒冈州和加利福尼亚州之间奔波，在公寓和房屋之间流转，在不同的继父母之间穿梭。

sentences.en: I've always been awed, anxious, introverted.
sentences.zh: 我一直是个充满敬畏、焦虑、内向的人。

sentences.en: I sometimes burst into tears at strange moments.
sentences.zh: 我有时会在奇怪的时刻突然放声大哭。

sentences.en: Lately, I've found myself thinking more and more of The Old Leather
sentences.zh: 最近，我发现自己越来越频繁地想起老皮匠

sentences.en: Man.
sentences.zh: 的故事。

sentences.en: The 21st century, unfortunately, turns out to be the perfect moment to be obsessed with his story.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，21世纪恰恰是迷恋他的故事的最佳时期。

sentences.en: America keeps spasming with increasing violence in many of the same ways it spasmed in the 1800s.
sentences.zh: 美国不断以越来越暴烈的方式发生痉挛，就像它在19世纪经历的那样。

sentences.en: The old leatherman looped his loops during an era of assassination, insurrection, civil war, impeachment, economic collapse, and racial terror.
sentences.zh: 老皮匠在暗杀、暴动、内战、弹劾、经济崩溃和种族恐怖的时代里周游穿梭。

sentences.en: He walked during the rise of Reconstruction and the crimes of so-called redemption.
sentences.zh: 他在重建时期崛起和所谓救赎罪恶的阴影中行走。

sentences.en: All around him, the landscape was being transformed.
sentences.zh: 在他周围的各处，地貌正在发生巨变。

sentences.en: Forests fell, church spires climbed, downtowns burned, and rose again.
sentences.zh: 森林倒下，教堂尖顶拔地而起，市中心化为焦土又再度重建。

sentences.en: He watched farms die, and railroads boom, and aqueducts stretch between cities.
sentences.zh: 他目睹了农场的消亡、铁路的兴隆，以及城市之间水渠的延展。

sentences.en: We have no idea what the old leather man thought of any of this, or if he thought of it at all.
sentences.zh: 我们完全无从得知老皮匠对这一切作何感想，或者他是否根本就没想过这些。

sentences.en: And that is exactly the point.
sentences.zh: 而这恰恰是关键所在。

sentences.en: All we know is that he kept walking.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的唯独只有他一直在走。

sentences.en: Every morning as I struggled to metabolize the daily news, I found myself dreaming of dropping out of society, following in his footsteps,
sentences.zh: 每天早晨，当我努力消化着每日的新闻时，我发现自己都在梦想着脱离社会，沿着他的足迹前行，

sentences.en: knocking on the doors he knocked on, sitting in the caves he sat in.
sentences.zh: 敲响他曾敲过的房门，坐在他曾坐过的洞穴里。

sentences.en: In the same way other people fantasized about moving to Canada, I fantasized about walking the old leather man's loop.
sentences.zh: 就像其他人幻想搬去加拿大一样，我幻想的是走完老皮匠的路线。

sentences.en: But how?
sentences.zh: 但是怎么走呢？

sentences.en: As a practical itinerary, the loop turned out to be tricky.
sentences.zh: 作为一条切实的行程路线，这条环路相当棘手。

sentences.en: It was regular, but also elusive.
sentences.zh: 它既有规律，又捉摸不定。

sentences.en: A network of highways, country lanes, backwoods trails, and railroad tracks that could shift subtly on his tiniest whim.
sentences.zh: 那是一个由公路、乡村小路、荒野小径和铁路线交织而成的网络，会随着他微不足道的突发奇想而微妙地改变。

sentences.en: Once, when one of his regular households got a pet dog, the old Leatherman never stopped there again.
sentences.zh: 有一次，当他常去的一户人家养了一只宠物狗后，老皮匠就再也没有去那里落脚。

sentences.en: As one of the great old Leatherman researchers, Allison Albee, has put it,
sentences.zh: 正如伟大的老皮匠研究者艾森·阿尔比所说的那样，

sentences.en: all effort to tie directions he is said to have followed into a single contiguous pattern seems utterly futile.
sentences.zh: 任何试图将他据称走过的方向串联成一个连续统一图案的努力，都显得彻底徒劳。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, I tried.
sentences.zh: 然而，我还是尝试了。

sentences.en: I visited research archives, made long lists, studied hand-drawn maps.
sentences.zh: 我走访了研究档案馆，列出长长的清单，研究手绘地图。

sentences.en: I tapped into the knowledge of other Old Leatherman obsessives
sentences.zh: 我借助了其他老皮匠痴迷者的智慧，

sentences.en: A scattered group of amateur enthusiasts
sentences.zh: 那是一群零星的业余爱好者，

sentences.en: Who've been stockpiling data points for 150 years I spoke with Steve Grant
sentences.zh: 他们150年来一直在囤积各种数据点。我采访了史蒂夫·格兰特，

sentences.en: A journalist who walked the Old Leatherman's loop For the Hartford Courant in 1993
sentences.zh: 他是一名记者，曾在1993年为《哈特福德courant报》走过老皮匠的路线

sentences.en: Grant told me with a real sense of loss That most of his maps are gone
sentences.zh: 格兰特带着一种真正的失落感告诉我，他的大部分地图都已经不见了

sentences.en: Years ago, some other Old Leathermanophile
sentences.zh: 多年前，另一个老皮匠狂热爱好者

sentences.en: Borrowed them and never gave them back I pored over an online cave guide compiled by Lee Stewart Evans, an outdoorsy Englishman transplanted to Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 借走后就再也没有还给他。我仔细研读了一份在线洞穴指南，该指南由移居康涅狄格州的户外运动英国人李·斯图尔特·埃文斯汇编。

sentences.en: And I basically wore out my copy of Dan W.
sentences.zh: 我还几乎把丹·W·

sentences.en: DeLuca's heroically thorough book, The Old Leatherman, Historical Accounts of a Connecticut and New York Legend.
sentences.zh: 德卢卡那本极其详尽的书《老皮匠：康涅狄格州与纽约州传奇的历史记录》翻烂了。

sentences.en: Eventually, I cobbled together what I thought was a reasonable outline of the loop.
sentences.zh: 最终，我拼凑出了一份自认为合理的路线大纲。

sentences.en: It was a bizarre travel itinerary, as if someone closed their eyes and drew with a shaky hand the most random possible cross-section of small northeastern towns.
sentences.zh: 这是一份古怪的旅行路线图，就像有人闭上眼睛用颤抖的手画出了东北部小镇中最随机的横截面。

sentences.en: There are once-bustling river ports like Ossining and Old Saybrook, and former manufacturing centers Bristol, Terryville, Plymouth,
sentences.zh: 那里有曾一度繁华的河港如奥西宁和老萨伯勒，以及昔日的制造业中心布里斯托尔、特里维尔、普利茅斯，

sentences.en: and destination antique shopping towns like Woodbury.
sentences.zh: 还有以古董购物闻名的目的地小镇伍德伯里。

sentences.en: You could live 1,000 very full lives and never think about any of these places.
sentences.zh: 你可以过一千种无比充实的人生，却也从未想过这些地方。

sentences.en: But that was also its appeal.
sentences.zh: 但这正是它的魅力所在。

sentences.en: There's nothing obvious about this route.
sentences.zh: 这条路线没有任何显而易见之处。

sentences.en: The old leather man was giving me an excuse to step outside my own life, to look at old American places firsthand, slowly, to think about how they had changed.
sentences.zh: 老皮匠给了我一个借口，让我能走出自己的生活，去亲眼、慢慢地审视古老的美国小镇，思考它们是如何发生变化的。

sentences.en: To walk around like a weirdo, knocking randomly on doors, talking to people who I had no business talking to.
sentences.zh: 像个怪人一样四处闲逛，随意敲门，和那些本不该有交集的人攀谈。

sentences.en: I just needed the right inspiration to start.
sentences.zh: 我只需要一个合适的灵感来启程。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Lowe.
sentences.zh: 我是韦娜·洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《Connections》这款游戏，它是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由那些人制作的，

sentences.en: like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: I started walking on November 6th, 2024.
sentences.zh: 我于2024年11月6日开始徒步。

sentences.en: For months, I realized I'd been living inside of screens, vibrating on poisonous frequencies.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，我意识到自己一直生活在屏幕里面，在有毒的频率中震颤。

sentences.en: And now the inside of my skull was itchy and all human language felt like packing peanuts in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 而现在我的头皮发痒，所有的人类语言在嘴里都感觉像是填充泡沫塑料。

sentences.en: I had a very strong impulse to move.
sentences.zh: 我有一种极其强烈的冲动想要离开。

sentences.en: So I grabbed a backpack and drove down to the old leatherman's grave
sentences.zh: 于是我抓起一个背包，开车前往老皮匠的墓地

sentences.en: The cemetery is just off the Hudson River in Austin, New York On a street called Revolutionary Road It is, by American standards, ancient
sentences.zh: 墓地位于纽约奥斯汀哈德逊河畔附近，在一条叫做革命路的街上。按美国的标准来看，它已经很古老了

sentences.en: The headstones are thin with fancy font and odd spellings And little carved pictures full of feeling
sentences.zh: 墓碑很薄，刻着花体字和奇怪的拼写，还有充满情感的小浮雕

sentences.en: The memorial to the old leatherman is a big rock with a plaque
sentences.zh: 老皮匠的纪念碑是一块带铭牌的大石头

sentences.en: My plan was to start here, at the end of his journey, and move clockwise, unspooling the story of his life.
sentences.zh: 我的计划是从这里——他旅程的终点开始，顺时针前进，剥茧抽丝般展开他的一生。

sentences.en: I stood there for a good, long, meditative while.
sentences.zh: 我在那里站了好一会儿，陷入沉思。

sentences.en: And then, like the old leather man, I walked.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像老皮匠一样，我迈开了脚步。

sentences.en: I walked north, toward downtown Ossining.
sentences.zh: 我向北走去，朝着奥西宁市中心进发。

sentences.en: The day was strangely warm, 80 degrees.
sentences.zh: 那天天气异常暖和，达到了华氏80度。

sentences.en: People's yards were full of leftover Halloween decorations.
sentences.zh: 人们的院子里到处都是留下的万圣节装饰品。

sentences.en: Giant skeletons, the Grim Reaper, demon pumpkins.
sentences.zh: 巨大的骷髅、死神、恶魔南瓜。

sentences.en: It was leaf season, so I tromped next to and sometimes on top of huge piles of crispy golden brown leaves.
sentences.zh: 正值落叶季节，所以我踩着、有时甚至是踏在巨大的干枯金褐色落叶堆上前进。

sentences.en: All the green life of the year, dead, heaped up on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 一年中所有的绿色生命都已消亡，堆积在路边。

sentences.en: I passed a historic tavern where George Washington might have slept.
sentences.zh: 我经过了一家历史悠久的酒馆，乔治·华盛顿可能在那里睡过觉。

sentences.en: I found a $10 bill on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 我在人行道上捡到了一张10美元的钞票。

sentences.en: In people's yards, I saw a Gadsden flag, don't tread on me, and a United States flag so tattered, it looked like it had been through the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 在人们的院子里，我看到了加兹登旗“别踩我”，以及一面破烂不堪的美国国旗，看起来就像经历过内战一样。

sentences.en: For the next several months, off and on, I walked.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，我断断续续地一直在走。

sentences.en: Day by day, I would load my backpack with hard-boiled eggs and gas station snacks, then trudge up roads toward the points of interest on my map.
sentences.zh: 日复一日，我的背包里装满了水煮蛋和加油站零食，然后迈着沉重的步伐顺着道路走向地图上的兴趣点。

sentences.en: From Ossining, I went to Briarcliff Manor, where one of the old Leatherman's caves still sits tucked into the middle of a neighborhood near a dead-end sign.
sentences.zh: 从奥西宁出发，我去了布赖克利夫曼，那里老皮匠的一个洞穴仍然隐蔽在死胡同标志附近的一个居民区中央。

sentences.en: Then to Chappaqua, where the Clintons live.
sentences.zh: 然后前往克林顿夫妇居住的查帕夸。

sentences.en: In Lewisboro, I walked past a house where the old Leatherman used to knock on the drainpipe so the owner would give him coffee and sandwiches.
sentences.zh: 在刘易斯伯勒，我走过一栋房子，老皮匠过去常常敲那里的排水管，好让主人给他咖啡和三明治。

sentences.en: I knocked.
sentences.zh: 我敲了门。

sentences.en: No one was home.
sentences.zh: 家里没人。

sentences.en: I passed a house where the old leather man felt so comfortable that he used to go inside to eat when the weather was bad.
sentences.zh: 我路过一栋房子，老皮匠在那里的感觉如此自在，以至于天气不好时他会进去吃东西。

sentences.en: Until one calamitous day, the family brought out a watermelon and set it on the table.
sentences.zh: 直到灾难性的一天，这家人拿出一个西瓜摆在桌上。

sentences.en: And the old leather man stood up and walked out and never stopped at their house again.
sentences.zh: 于是老皮匠站起身走了出去，从此再也没有在他们家停留过。

sentences.en: I walked 13 miles one day, 15 miles another day, 18 miles, 20 miles.
sentences.zh: 有一天我走了13英里，另一天15英里，然后18英里，20英里。

sentences.en: In Woodbury, I walked to the site of Alexander Gordon Sr.'s tannery, where the old leatherman used to stop to collect leather scraps and drink from the water trough,
sentences.zh: 在伍德伯里，我走到了老亚历山大·戈登制革厂的遗址，老皮匠过去常在那里搜集皮革碎料并在水槽喝水，

sentences.en: and where he once allowed Gordon to oil up his suit.
sentences.zh: 并且有一次他在那里允许戈登给他的衣服上油。

sentences.en: It's now a liquor store.
sentences.zh: 这里现在是一家酒类专卖店。

sentences.en: Very slowly, clockwise, I crawled around the loop on my big giant map.
sentences.zh: 我非常缓慢地、顺时针地在我巨大的地图上的环路上爬行。

sentences.en: I have to say, right away, walking made me feel better.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，步行立刻让我感觉好多了。

sentences.en: Every morning, when I stepped onto the road, I got a little less angry.
sentences.zh: 每天早晨，当我踏上路途时，我的愤怒就会减少一点。

sentences.en: It's easy to hate the world when it's just an abstraction that lives in your phone.
sentences.zh: 当世界只存在于你手机里的一个抽象概念时，去恨它很容易。

sentences.en: It's harder when you're out there in it, really looking, interacting.
sentences.zh: 而当你真正身处其中、去审视、去互动时，这就变得很难了。

sentences.en: Tiny moments felt hugely healing.
sentences.zh: 那些微小的时刻有着巨大的治愈力量。

sentences.en: On the edge of Austin-ing, a woman at a gas station called out, asking if I would help her with something.
sentences.zh: 在奥斯汀市边缘，加油站的一个女人喊住我，问我能不能帮她个忙。

sentences.en: And I was sure it was going to be some kind of scam.
sentences.zh: 我当时确信这肯定是什么骗局之类的。

sentences.en: But it turned out she just couldn't figure out how to get her gas cap back on.
sentences.zh: 但结果证明她只是不知道怎么把油箱盖拧回去。

sentences.en: And I helped her.
sentences.zh: 我帮了她。

sentences.en: And she said, thank you for your kindness.
sentences.zh: 她说，谢谢你的善良。

sentences.en: I felt relieved to be living in reality again, following the small rhythm of my legs over the big rhythm of the landscape, noticing the world, the houses under the clouds.
sentences.zh: 我感到一种如释重负的解脱，能够再次生活在现实中，跟随双腿的小节奏感受风景的大节奏，留意着世界，留意着云层之下的房屋。

sentences.en: Block by block, mile by mile, I felt my soul begin to unclench, like one of those mattresses that get shipped super compressed in a tiny box.
sentences.zh: 一个街区接一个街区，一英里接一英里，我感觉到自己的灵魂开始放松开来，就像那些在小盒子里被超级压缩的床垫一样。

sentences.en: Stepping into the world opened the box.
sentences.zh: 踏入世界便打开了这个盒子。

sentences.en: Step by step, as the days and weeks passed, I felt my crushed soul stretching out to find its dimensions, expanding to fill the huge space of the whole expanding universe.
sentences.zh: 随着日子和星期的流逝，我一步步地感觉到我那饱受摧残的灵魂正在舒展开来以寻找它的维度，不断膨胀以填满整个不断扩张的宇宙的巨大空间。

sentences.en: I marveled again and again at the way the past and present sit on top of each other.
sentences.zh: 我一次又一次地惊叹于过去与现在交叠并存的方式。

sentences.en: I walked past 18th century mansions with electric gates and private basketball courts.
sentences.zh: 我走过装有电动大门和私人篮球场的18世纪豪宅。

sentences.en: I saw decrepit houses that looked held together more by air than by wood.
sentences.zh: 我看到破败的房屋，看起来与其说是靠木头支撑，不如说是靠空气撑着。

sentences.en: I ate a Ben and Jerry's ice cream cone while sitting on a rock where George Washington once allegedly ate his dinner.
sentences.zh: 我坐在据说乔治·华盛顿曾吃过晚饭的石头上，吃着一个本杰瑞冰激凌甜筒。

sentences.en: One day I stood staring fascinated at a decrepit brick house built in 1790, its windows broken in a way that made it look somehow like the
sentences.zh: 有一天，我盯着一栋建于1790年的破败砖房出神，它的窗户破碎的模样，某种程度上看起来就像是

sentences.en: embodiment of the fall of the American empire.
sentences.zh: 美利坚帝国衰落的化身。

sentences.en: And as I stood there, a cyber truck drove by.
sentences.zh: 就在我站在那里的时候，一辆赛博皮卡从旁边驶过。

sentences.en: On some days, the walking was heartbreakingly lovely.
sentences.zh: 有些日子，徒步之旅美得让人心碎。

sentences.en: The names of certain roads still make me sigh.
sentences.zh: 某些道路的名字依然让我发出叹息。

sentences.en: Wood Road, Gage Road, Spring Lake Road, Judds Bridge Road.
sentences.zh: 伍德路、盖奇路、斯普林湖路、贾兹布里奇路。

sentences.en: Huge territories felt like outdoor museuMs. Curated collections of old stone walls, curving gently and rising with the land.
sentences.zh: 广袤的领地感觉就像是户外博物馆，是由古老石墙构成的精心策展的藏品，它们与地势一同柔和地弯曲并起伏着。

sentences.en: The wide, quiet beauty of old New England.
sentences.zh: 新英格兰古老而开阔、宁静的美。

sentences.en: I spent many hours alone with birds.
sentences.zh: 我与鸟儿们度过了许多孤独的时光。

sentences.en: I watched a giant woodpecker perched on a thin, rotten tree, pecking so hard that the whole tree shook and
sentences.zh: 我看着一只巨大的啄木鸟栖息在一棵纤细的枯树上，啄得如此猛烈，以至于整棵树都在晃动摇摆，

sentences.en: swayed, pumping its red head until giant chunks of bark flew off, and it looked like the woodpecker was about to peck the whole thing apart and go plunging to the ground.
sentences.zh: 它那红色的脑袋上下泵动，直到大块的树皮飞落，看上去啄木鸟随时会把整棵树啄碎然后坠向地面。

sentences.en: Hawks screamed at me for invading their space, or they glided silently over my head, staring down.
sentences.zh: 老鹰对我入侵它们的领地发出尖叫，或者静静地从我头顶滑翔而过，居高临下地注视着。

sentences.en: I startled probably
sentences.zh: 我大概惊吓到了

sentences.en: 10,000 squirrels, and as they shot off through the dry leaves, they were so disproportionately loud that sometimes I thought they were bears.
sentences.zh: 一万只松鼠，当它们在枯叶中箭一般窜出去时，声音大得离谱，有时我都以为那是熊。

sentences.en: I had plenty of bad times, too.
sentences.zh: 我也经历过许多糟糕的时刻。

sentences.en: There were days so cold my hands stung, even in gloves, inside my coat pockets, and the wind whipped up tornadoes of snow, and I could feel my mustache hairs freezing and crunching
sentences.zh: 有些日子天气冷得刺骨，即便戴着手套、把手揣进大衣口袋里，双手依然生疼，风卷起阵阵雪龙卷，我甚至能感觉到鼻胡子的冰碴在鼻尖的哈气中冻结、碎裂

sentences.en: in the steam from my nose.
sentences.zh: 的声音。

sentences.en: Other days, just as cold, I was sweating so hard I had to take off my coat and hat.
sentences.zh: 还有些日子，同样寒冷，但我却汗流浃背，不得不脱掉大衣和帽子。

sentences.en: I was reminded over and over that the modern world is not made for walking.
sentences.zh: 我一次又一次地被提醒，现代世界并不是为步行而设计的。

sentences.en: I spent many miles trudging on high alert up traffic-y highways without shoulders.
sentences.zh: 我花了好几英里艰难地在没有路肩、车流量大的高速公路上高度戒备地跋涉。

sentences.en: Cars came screaming around corners.
sentences.zh: 汽车呼啸着转过弯角。

sentences.en: I found myself tightrope-walking along the tops of cliffs, clinging like a goat to the sides of hills, teetering on old stone walls.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在悬崖顶端走钢丝，像山羊一样紧紧抓着山坡的侧面，在古老的石墙上摇摇晃晃。

sentences.en: I stepped over all kinds of roadkill, a freshly pressed groundhog, a pancaked hawk,
sentences.zh: 我跨过各种各样的路死动物，一只刚被压扁的土拨鼠，一只被压成煎饼的老鹰，

sentences.en: A pickup truck speeding passed so close that I felt a rush of wind, and at the last second a German shepherd shot its head out the window, barking and snapping,
sentences.zh: 一辆皮卡呼啸着贴身驶过，让我感受到了一股气流，千钧一发之际，一只德国牧羊犬把头探出窗外，狂吠并龇牙咧嘴，

sentences.en: actually trying to bite me.
sentences.zh: 实际上是想咬我。

sentences.en: One car whipped around a blind turn so suddenly that I went leaping over a guardrail, bashing my shin.
sentences.zh: 有一辆汽车突然猛拐过盲弯，吓得我直接跳过护栏，撞伤了小腿胫骨。

sentences.en: It left a swollen knot that's still there.
sentences.zh: 那留下了一个肿包，到现在都还在。

sentences.en: That same day, fighting my way through roadside trees, clinging to a different guardrail for balance, I sliced the heel of my hand open on a nasty piece of metal.
sentences.zh: 就在同一天，当我挣扎着穿过路边的树木、死死抓住另一处护栏保持平衡时，我的手掌跟被一块恶劣的金属片划开了一个大口子。

sentences.en: It became clear to me very quickly that, despite my fascination and my fantasies, I am not the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 我很快就清楚地意识到，尽管我充满了着迷和幻想，但我并不是老皮匠。

sentences.en: I never slept in a cave.
sentences.zh: 我从没在洞穴里睡过觉。

sentences.en: In fact, it turns out that I'm afraid of caves.
sentences.zh: 事实上，事实证明我其实很怕洞穴。

sentences.en: Every time I found one, I would stand outside it for a few minutes, trying to peer in from a distance, and then I'd throw in rocks and sticks to scare out any wild animals.
sentences.zh: 每次我发现一个洞穴，我都会在外面站上几分钟，试图从远处往里窥视，然后我会往里面扔石头和棍子来惊吓任何可能存在的野生动物。

sentences.en: And only then, cautiously, holding my breath, would I creep inside.
sentences.zh: 只有在那个时候，我才会屏住呼吸、小心翼翼地潜进去。

sentences.en: Instead, I slept in hotels.
sentences.zh: 相反，我都住在酒店里。

sentences.en: Or I just went home.
sentences.zh: 或者我直接回家。

sentences.en: I'd walk all day and then, exhausted, order an Uber back to wherever I'd started, usually a shopping center where I'd parked my car.
sentences.zh: 我走上一整天，然后精疲力竭地叫一辆优步回到我出发的地方，通常是我停放汽车的购物中心。

sentences.en: The ride was always humiliating.
sentences.zh: 这段车程总是让人感到羞辱。

sentences.en: In 10 or 15 minutes, it rewound the walk that had taken me all day.
sentences.zh: 只需10到15分钟，它就把我走了一整天的路给倒放了回去。

sentences.en: It turned out that I was much more a creature of society than I like to admit.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我比自己愿意承认的要更具社会属性。

sentences.en: I'd walk for a couple of days and then have to go home for a dentist appointment.
sentences.zh: 我走上几天，然后就得回家去看牙医。

sentences.en: Things wouldn't stop coming up.
sentences.zh: 各种事情总是接踵而至。

sentences.en: I took breaks from the loop because my daughter was visiting for Christmas, because I got a nasty head cold, because my beloved wiener dog, Walnut,
sentences.zh: 我从环线中抽身休息，因为女儿圣诞节来访，因为我得了严重的重感冒，因为我深爱的腊肠犬“核桃”，

sentences.en: suddenly lost the use of his back legs, and we thought he was about to die.
sentences.zh: 突然失去了后腿的知觉，我们以为他快要死了。

sentences.en: He got better.
sentences.zh: 他好转了。

sentences.en: One evening, at the end of a particularly grueling 20-mile walk, my wife picked me up in front of a public library, and we went out for Thai food.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，在结束了一场格外折磨人的20英里徒步后，妻子在公共图书馆门前接了我，我们一起去吃泰餐。

sentences.en: She liked to call me the old pleather man.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢叫我老皮革人。

sentences.en: Yet, over many weeks, after maybe 100 miles of walking, my domestication started to wear off.
sentences.zh: 然而，在许多个星期、走了大约100英里之后，我的驯化开始逐渐消退。

sentences.en: One night I came home after a few days on the road, after not changing my clothes, and everyone in the house stiffened.
sentences.zh: 一天夜里，我在路上走了几天、没换衣服就回了家，家里所有人都紧绷了起来。

sentences.en: My smell was like I'd brought a whole other person home with me, someone none of us had met before.
sentences.zh: 我的气味就像带了另一个完全陌生的人回家，一个谁都没见过的人。

sentences.en: One Tuesday, in mid-January, I reached a man-made lake the old leather man never would have seen.
sentences.zh: 一月中旬的一个星期二，我到达了一个人工湖，这是当年的老皮革人永远也见不到的。

sentences.en: In his time, it was a river winding through a town, until they dammed it two years after his death to provide drinking water for New York City.
sentences.zh: 在他那个时代，这里只是一条蜿蜒穿过小镇的河流，直到在他去世两年后，人们为了给纽约市提供饮用水而筑坝蓄水。

sentences.en: Today, it is the East Branch Reservoir.
sentences.zh: 如今，这里是东支水库。

sentences.en: When its surface is low, you can still see the old foundations of flooded buildings.
sentences.zh: 当水位较低时，你仍然可以看到被淹没建筑物的旧地基。

sentences.en: I walked on its shore over honeycombs of dried mud.
sentences.zh: 我走在它的岸边，脚下是蜂窝状的干涸泥地。

sentences.en: The water was frozen.
sentences.zh: 水面已经结冰。

sentences.en: Way out in the distance, on the surface,
sentences.zh: 在极远的远处，冰面上，

sentences.en: I noticed tiny shapes moving.
sentences.zh: 我注意到有微小的形状在移动。

sentences.en: Ice fishermen.
sentences.zh: 冰上垂钓者。

sentences.en: I stepped out.
sentences.zh: 我走了过去。

sentences.en: cautiously, arms spread, and stood watching a man drill a fresh hole in the ice with a bright orange auger.
sentences.zh: 小心翼翼地张开双臂，站在那里看着一个男人用亮橙色的螺旋钻在冰面上钻出一个新洞。

sentences.en: When he was done, I asked him if he'd ever heard of the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 他弄完后，我问他是否听说过老皮革人。

sentences.en: Of course, he said.
sentences.zh: 当然，他说。

sentences.en: Everyone knew about the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道老皮革人。

sentences.en: Used to walk around, sleep in caves.
sentences.zh: 过去常常到处走，睡在山洞里。

sentences.en: Back in those days, the man said, that kind of lifestyle wasn't so unusual.
sentences.zh: 那个人说，在那个年代，那种生活方式并非那么罕见。

sentences.en: People were more comfortable outside.
sentences.zh: 人们在户外感觉更自在。

sentences.en: In fact, he told me, even when he was young, growing up right near this reservoir, there were people who lived like that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他告诉我，甚至在他小时候，在紧邻这个水库的地方长大时，也有那样生活的人。

sentences.en: One of them slept in the woods near his family's house.
sentences.zh: 其中一个就睡他家附近的树林里。

sentences.en: An alcoholic, friendly and harmless.
sentences.zh: 是个酒鬼，友善且无害。

sentences.en: He remembers going out as a kid to give the man bacon.
sentences.zh: 他记得自己小时候跑出去给那个人送培根。

sentences.en: On my walks, this kind of conversation was surprisingly common.
sentences.zh: 在我的徒步过程中，这种对话出奇地普遍。

sentences.en: I would ask people about the old leather man, and they would end up telling me about some other figure who once lived on the fringes of society.
sentences.zh: 我会向人们询问老皮革人的事，而他们最后总会告诉我一些曾经生活在社会边缘的其他人物。

sentences.en: One woman told me about a guy named
sentences.zh: 有个女人跟我说起一个叫

sentences.en: Footsie who used to walk around Watertown, Connecticut back in her father's time.
sentences.zh: 富蒂（Footsie）的家伙，在她父亲的年代，他经常在康涅狄格州沃特敦四处游荡。

sentences.en: Several people mentioned the tragic life of Sarah Bishop, a young American who was kidnapped
sentences.zh: 几个人提到了萨拉·毕晓普（Sarah Bishop）悲惨的一生，这位年轻的美国女性在

sentences.en: during the Revolutionary War by British pirates, only to escape and live the rest of her life alone in a mountain cave.
sentences.zh: 独立战争期间被英国海盗绑架，后来逃脱，并在山洞里孤身一人度过了余生。

sentences.en: I heard about mythic figures, the Witch of Good Hill, the Green Lady of Burlington, some of whom still haunt the places where they died.
sentences.zh: 我听说过一些神话般的人物，古德希尔女巫、伯灵顿绿衣女郎，其中有些人至今仍在他们死去的地方徘徊。

sentences.en: Haunting, I think, is a nice metaphor for the social dynamics here.
sentences.zh: 我想，徘徊是这里社会动态的一个绝佳隐喻。

sentences.en: An in-group is haunted, more or less permanently, by the people it chooses to exclude.
sentences.zh: 一个内群体多多少少会永久地被它选择排斥的人所纠缠。

sentences.en: They hang around like obtrusive thoughts.
sentences.zh: 他们像挥之不去的杂念一样盘桓不去。

sentences.en: And in the old Leatherman's time, New England was a deeply haunted place.
sentences.zh: 在老皮革人的时代，新英格兰是一个充满了幽灵般记忆的地方。

sentences.en: After the Civil War, especially during the Depression of the 1870s,
sentences.zh: 内战结束后，特别是经历了1873年的经济大萧条之后，

sentences.en: There was a widespread public panic about so-called tramps, unemployed men roaming by the thousands, begging, hopping trains, looking for work.
sentences.zh: 公众对所谓的流浪汉产生了广泛的恐慌——成千上万的失业男子四处游荡、乞讨、扒乘火车、寻找工作。

sentences.en: The rhetoric in the newspapers about, quote, robbery, incendiarism, intimidation, rape and murder will sound familiar to modern readers.
sentences.zh: 报纸上关于诸如“抢劫、纵火、恐吓、强奸和谋杀”的言论，现代读者听起来会觉得似曾相识。

sentences.en: In Bristol, a writer declared that the solution was vigilante violence, a trusty weapon in every house, they wrote, and a disposition to use it on very slight provocation.
sentences.zh: 在布里斯托尔，一位作家宣称解决方案是民兵暴力，他们写道，每家每户都应备有一把可靠的武器，并准备在受到微小挑衅时就使用它。

sentences.en: Eventually,
sentences.zh: 最终，

sentences.en: Connecticut passed a strict anti-tramp law mandating the appointment of special constables
sentences.zh: 康涅狄格州通过了一项严厉的反流浪法，规定任命特别警长

sentences.en: to hunt vagrants down, promising $5 bounties for warrantless arrests resulting in conviction.
sentences.zh: 来追捕流浪者，并承诺对无需搜查令的逮捕且最终定罪的行为给予5美元的悬赏。

sentences.en: In this atmosphere, even the old leather man was suspect.
sentences.zh: 在这种氛围下，连老皮革人也受到了怀疑。

sentences.en: Early in his wanderings, people locked their doors when he passed.
sentences.zh: 在他流浪的早期，人们在他路过时会锁上房门。

sentences.en: Mothers used him as a kind of boogeyman to make their children behave.
sentences.zh: 母亲们把他当成一种莫须有的妖怪来吓唬不听话的孩子。

sentences.en: But although he looked terrifying, people quickly came to understand that he was harmless.
sentences.zh: 但尽管他看起来很吓人，人们很快就明白他是无害的。

sentences.en: He never stole, never created chaos, never accosted anyone.
sentences.zh: 他从不偷窃，从不制造混乱，也从未搭讪任何人。

sentences.en: Even when he was actively harassed, when a group of children surrounded him in the street shouting insults, or when two rowdy men bullied him forcing him to drink alcohol,
sentences.zh: 甚至当他遭到积极的骚扰时——当一群孩子在街上围着他大声辱骂，或者当两个粗鲁的男子欺负他、强迫他喝酒时，

sentences.en: The old Leatherman didn't fight back.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人也没有还手。

sentences.en: He just got away as quickly as he could.
sentences.zh: 他只是尽快逃离。

sentences.en: He was quiet and inoffensive, said a man who saw him regularly near Waterbury.
sentences.zh: 一个经常在沃特伯里附近看到他的人说，他安静而无害。

sentences.en: And when a person came along driving a lively horse, he would get out of the way so that his odd appearance might not frighten the horse.
sentences.zh: 当有人驾着一匹性情急躁的马过来时，他会主动避让，以免自己古怪的外表吓到马。

sentences.en: Soon, all across old Leatherman territory, a communal instinct kicked in.
sentences.zh: 很快，在老皮革人出没的整个地区，一种共同的本能被激发了。

sentences.en: Residents didn't just tolerate him.
sentences.zh: 居民们不仅容忍他。

sentences.en: They protected him.
sentences.zh: 他们保护他。

sentences.en: They took pride in his visits.
sentences.zh: 他们以他的造访为傲。

sentences.en: They made special food to prepare for his arrival.
sentences.zh: 他们为他的到来准备特殊的食物。

sentences.en: Mothers scolded children for staring at him in the street.
sentences.zh: 母亲们会责备那些在街上盯着他看的孩子。

sentences.en: One boy, out for a hike, found an old Leatherman cave unoccupied and used the wood inside to make a fire.
sentences.zh: 有个男孩出去远足时，发现了一个空无一人的老皮革人山洞，并用里面的木头生了火。

sentences.en: When he got home, his mother made him go back, in the dark, to replenish the wood.
sentences.zh: 等他回到家，母亲逼着他在黑暗中走回去，把木头补上。

sentences.en: She didn't want the old Leatherman to get cold.
sentences.zh: 她不想让老皮革人受冻。

sentences.en: The townspeople regarded the old Leatherman with a mix of closeness and distance, familiarity and alienation.
sentences.zh: 镇民们以一种亲密与疏离、熟悉与陌生交织的目光看待老皮革人。

sentences.en: He was the insider's outsider.
sentences.zh: 他是圈内人的圈外人。

sentences.en: He didn't belong, but he was accepted.
sentences.zh: 他不属于这里，但他被接受了。

sentences.en: Wherever he went, he created a circle of civility.
sentences.zh: 无论他走到哪里，他都营造出一个礼貌的圈子。

sentences.en: His loop tied together otherwise disparate communities, like beads on a string.
sentences.zh: 他的环线将原本毫无关联的社区串联在一起，就像线上的珍珠一样。

sentences.en: The tramp laws, curiously, didn't seem to apply to him.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，流浪汉法似乎并不适用于他。

sentences.en: By tramping so openly, he seemed to transcend the category.
sentences.zh: 由于如此公开地流浪，他似乎超越了这一类别。

sentences.en: He was his own special category.
sentences.zh: 他自成一类。

sentences.en: He was the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 他就是老皮革人。

sentences.en: Maybe my favorite incident in the old leather man story happened in a small town called Shrub Oak.
sentences.zh: 关于老皮革人的故事中，我最喜欢的插曲可能发生在压木村（Shrub Oak）这个小镇上。

sentences.en: He had multiple admirers there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里有很多崇拜者。

sentences.en: One family, the Ireland's, kept a special bowl and spoon just to feed him.
sentences.zh: 有一家人，即爱尔兰一家，专门留了一个碗和一个勺子用来喂他。

sentences.en: Down the street, at Darrow's grocery store, the owner kept notes in his account book about the old Leatherman's trips through town.
sentences.zh: 顺着街往下走，在达罗的杂货店里，店主在他的记账本里记录了老皮革人途经镇上的情况。

sentences.en: In February 1885, when the old Leatherman didn't show up on schedule, the people of Shrub Oak were worried.
sentences.zh: 1885年2月，当老皮革人没有按时出现时，压木村的人们开始担心起来。

sentences.en: The weather had been terrible.
sentences.zh: 天气实在太恶劣了。

sentences.en: Weeks of sub-freezing temperatures.
sentences.zh: 连续数周气温低于冰点。

sentences.en: Brutal rain.
sentences.zh: 残酷的阴雨。

sentences.en: A group went out to check his cave in the woods near the ruins of a sawmill.
sentences.zh: 一群人前往锯木厂遗迹附近的树林里查看他的山洞。

sentences.en: It was empty.
sentences.zh: 里面空无一人。

sentences.en: So it was a relief when, on Thursday, February 19th, Darrow, standing in his store, saw the old leather man clomping up the street.
sentences.zh: 因此，当2月19日星期四，达罗站在店里看到老皮革人踏着沉重的脚步走上街头时，大家终于松了一口气。

sentences.en: He was several days late and seemed to be in a hurry, trying to make up for lost time.
sentences.zh: 他迟到了几天，而且似乎行色匆匆，试图弥补失去的时间。

sentences.en: Darrow called out.
sentences.zh: 达罗大声喊他。

sentences.en: He motioned to the old leather man to come inside, and against all odds, for reasons no one could fathom, the old leather man did.
sentences.zh: 他示意老皮革人进来，出乎所有人意料的是，出于谁也猜不透的原因，老皮革人真的进来了。

sentences.en: He sat down next to the fire.
sentences.zh: 他在火炉旁坐了下来。

sentences.en: Mr. Darrow gave him some cheese and crackers, and as he watched the old leather man eat, he decided to try something.
sentences.zh: 达罗先生给了他一些奶酪和饼干，看着老皮革人吃东西时，他决定尝试一件事情。

sentences.en: He took out a pencil and a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 他拿出一支铅笔和一张纸。

sentences.en: I am old, Darrow said, and he wrote down his age.
sentences.zh: “我很老了，”达罗说着，写下了自己的年龄。

sentences.en: Then he passed the paper and pencil to the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 然后他把纸和铅笔递给老皮革人。

sentences.en: How old are you?
sentences.zh: “你多大了？”

sentences.en: he asked.
sentences.zh: 他问。

sentences.en: People had been trying and failing for many years to pry information out of the old leather man.
sentences.zh: 多年来，人们一直试图从老皮革人那里套出信息，但都失败了。

sentences.en: Sometimes he grunted or muttered a few words in what some people claimed was French.
sentences.zh: 有时他会发出咕哝声，或者用一些人声称是法语的语言嘟囔几句。

sentences.en: Mostly, he just turned and walked away.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，他只是转身走开。

sentences.en: But this time, according to the shopkeeper, he didn't.
sentences.zh: 但据这位店主说，这一次他没有。

sentences.en: The old leather man took the pencil and pressed it to the paper.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人接过铅笔，将其按在纸上。

sentences.en: In large, crooked strokes, he wrote a string of numbers.
sentences.zh: 他用大大的、歪歪扭扭的笔画写下一串数字。

sentences.en: A few days later, the Peekskill Blade printed a facsimile of this odd answer, just as the old Leatherman wrote it.
sentences.zh: 几天后，《皮克斯基尔刀锋报》（Peekskill Blade）印刷了这个古怪答案的摹本，完全照着老皮革人写的那样。

sentences.en: What did it mean?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？

sentences.en: There were debates.
sentences.zh: 人们展开了争论。

sentences.en: Some thought the old Leatherman must have been writing his birthday in the European style,
sentences.zh: 有人认为老皮革人当时一定是用欧洲风格写下他的生日，

sentences.en: This would have made him 42 years old.
sentences.zh: 这样的话他当时就是42岁。

sentences.en: Some, drunk on the mythology of the old Leatherman, took it at face value, as evidence that he was 15,342 years old.
sentences.zh: 有些人沉迷于老皮革人的神话，将其字面理解为他已经活了15342岁的证据。

sentences.en: Decades later, the researcher Allison Albee offered this speculation
sentences.zh: 几十年后，研究员埃里森·阿尔比（Allison Albee）提出了这样一种推测：

sentences.en: One guess, being as good as another
sentences.zh: 一种猜测与其他猜测同样合理——

sentences.en: Perhaps the Leatherman, understanding neither the question
sentences.zh: 也许皮革人既不懂这个问题，

sentences.en: Nor the meaning of Mr. Darrow's figures
sentences.zh: 也不懂达罗先生那些数字的含义，

sentences.en: Showed his own peculiar method of writing
sentences.zh: 只是展示了他自己独特的书写方式：

sentences.en: Or maybe it was some kind of inscrutable code
sentences.zh: 或者这可能是某种高深莫测的代码。

sentences.en: This to me is the perfect old Leatherman story an absurdly specific data point with no clear explanation.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这就是最完美的老皮革人故事——一个荒谬具体、毫无明确解释的数据点。

sentences.en: We know plenty of facts about him.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了关于他的大量事实。

sentences.en: His height, roughly 5'7", the weight of his suit, 60 pounds, the length of his homemade hatchet blade,
sentences.zh: 他的身高大约是5尺7寸，他那套衣服重60磅，他自制手斧的刀刃长度是

sentences.en: 9 1⁄4 inches.
And yet, the man himself was, is, and probably always will be a mystery.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个人本身过去、现在、并且可能永远都是一个谜。

sentences.en: This is what I love, what keeps me circling back to him over and over.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所热爱的，也是让我一次又一次回味他的原因。

sentences.en: The Old Leatherman is an engine of infinite interpretations, a story about stories.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人是一个无限解读的引擎，一个关于故事的故事。

sentences.en: He gave us so little, and in doing so, he gave us so much.
sentences.zh: 他给我们的如此之少，而在此过程中，他又给予了我们如此之多。

sentences.en: In the 19th century, he was a perfect blank screen onto which society could project its fears and fantasies.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，他是一块完美的空白屏幕，社会可以在上面投射其恐惧和幻想。

sentences.en: And he remains so today.
sentences.zh: 今天依然如此。

sentences.en: This is the real Old Leatherman's loop.
sentences.zh: 这就是真正的老皮革人环线。

sentences.en: The one that we all walk, every second, on every level, eternally.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在每一个秒钟、每一个层面、永恒地走着的那条环线。

sentences.en: The loop between reality and meaning.
sentences.zh: 现实与意义之间的环线。

sentences.en: What we know and what we imagine.
sentences.zh: 我们所知的与我们所想象的。

sentences.en: The old Leatherman's last loop came in March 1889.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人的最后一条环线始于1889年3月。

sentences.en: For months, it had been clear that something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，很明显有些不对劲。

sentences.en: The old Leatherman was sick.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人病了。

sentences.en: In the later photos, you can see it.
sentences.zh: 从后期的照片中，你能看出来。

sentences.en: His bottom lip is swollen, marred by what one writer described as a raw sore.
sentences.zh: 他的下唇肿胀，被一位作家描述为“生红的溃疡”所毁坏。

sentences.en: This was almost definitely mouth cancer, almost definitely from the tobacco that he liked to either chew or to smoke in his homemade pipe.
sentences.zh: 这几乎肯定是口腔癌，几乎肯定来自他喜欢咀嚼或在自制烟斗里抽的烟草。

sentences.en: The old leather man would often stoop down in front of post offices and general stores to pick up cigarette butts that people had thrown in the dirt.
sentences.zh: 老皮革人经常会弯腰在邮局和杂货店门前捡起人们扔在泥土里的烟头。

sentences.en: When he ate, he covered the sore with a special patch of leather.
sentences.zh: 他吃东西时，会用一块特殊的皮革补丁盖住溃疡。

sentences.en: One house he stopped at for breakfast belonged to a doctor, and the old Leatherman allowed him to examine his lip.
sentences.zh: 他驻足吃早餐的一所房子属于一位医生，老皮革人允许他检查自己的嘴唇。

sentences.en: The doctor gave him some ointment.
sentences.zh: 医生给了他一些药膏。

sentences.en: But things got worse.
sentences.zh: 但情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: The sore deepened into a hole that eventually ate away half of the old Leatherman's jaw.
sentences.zh: 溃疡恶化成了一个洞，最终侵蚀掉了老皮革人的一半下巴。

sentences.en: He could hardly eat.
sentences.zh: 他几乎无法进食。

sentences.en: He had to soak his food in coffee, then drink it.
sentences.zh: 他不得不把食物泡在咖啡里，然后喝下去。

sentences.en: And some of it would come pouring right through his face.
sentences.zh: 有些食物甚至会直接从他的面部漏出来。

sentences.en: His walking got slower and slower.
sentences.zh: 他的步伐越来越慢。

sentences.en: He began to lose weight.
sentences.zh: 他开始瘦了。

sentences.en: Still, he kept going.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他还是坚持走下去。

sentences.en: Finally, people along his loop decided to try something drastic.
sentences.zh: 最终，他巡回路线沿途的人们决定采取一些极端的措施。

sentences.en: In Middletown, Connecticut, residents set up a sort of sting operation.
sentences.zh: 在康涅狄格州米德尔敦，居民们设下了一个类似钓鱼执法局的圈套。

sentences.en: When the old Leatherman stopped for a meal, as he always did at the house of Amy Guy, she sent a messenger two miles up the road to his next stop, the Fisher House.
sentences.zh: 当老皮鞋人停下来吃饭时，就像他在艾米·盖伊家一直做的那样，艾米派了一个信使沿着公路走了两英里，去通知他的下一站费舍尔家。

sentences.en: When the old Leatherman showed up there, he encountered a group of strangers,
sentences.zh: 当老皮鞋人出现在那里时，他遇到了一群陌生人，

sentences.en: The police chief, the town physician, some representatives of the Connecticut Humane Society.
sentences.zh: 警察局长、镇上的医生，还有康涅狄格州人道协会的一些代表。

sentences.en: They basically arrested him, benevolently, and got him into a carriage.
sentences.zh: 他们出于好意，基本上可以说是把他“逮捕”了，并把他扶上一辆马车。

sentences.en: According to one of the Fishers, he went with no reluctance and seemed to understand why, though the conversation was carried on by signs, mostly.
sentences.zh: 据其中一位费舍尔家人回忆，他非常顺从，似乎明白为什么要这么做，尽管大家的交流主要靠手势。

sentences.en: The old leatherman was driven to the Hartford Hospital.
sentences.zh: 老皮鞋人被带到了哈特福德医院。

sentences.en: Maybe the doctors there could save his life, or at least ease his suffering.
sentences.zh: 也许那里的医生能救他的命，或者至少能减轻他的痛苦。

sentences.en: But he refused to stay.
sentences.zh: 但他拒绝留下来。

sentences.en: Soon after he was dropped off, the old leather man walked out.
sentences.zh: 他刚被放下车没多久，老皮鞋人就走了出去。

sentences.en: He went right back to his loop.
sentences.zh: 他径直回到了自己的路线上。

sentences.en: A week later, in very bad shape, he showed up for dinner at the Barnard House in North Haven, 30 miles from Hartford.
sentences.zh: 一周后，状态极差的他出现在北黑文巴纳德之家的餐厅里，这里距离哈特福德有30英里。

sentences.en: He was muddy and wet.
sentences.zh: 他浑身泥泞，湿漉漉的。

sentences.en: They managed to coax him inside, next to the fire.
sentences.zh: 他们设法哄他进屋，在火炉旁坐下。

sentences.en: They offered him an apple, but he just pointed to his lip and shook his head.
sentences.zh: 他们递给他一个苹果，但他只是指了指自己的嘴唇，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: Instead, he drank six large bowls of coffee-soaked food, bread, cake, pie.
sentences.zh: 相反，他喝了六大碗泡在咖啡里的食物——面包、蛋糕和馅饼。

sentences.en: He was told to sit and warm himself as long as he liked, the Hartford Times reported later.
sentences.zh: 《哈特福德时报》后来报道说，人们告诉他想坐多久就坐多久，好好暖和一下。

sentences.en: He simply pointed up the road and, with an expressive gesture, indicated that he must go.
sentences.zh: 他只是向前方的路指了指，通过一个传神的动作，示意他必须走了。

sentences.en: That was in December.
sentences.zh: 那是十二月。

sentences.en: In mid-March, the old leatherman was seen heading in the direction of Ossining.
sentences.zh: 三月中旬，有人看到老皮鞋人朝着奥西宁的方向走去。

sentences.en: He was so weak by this point that he had to sit and rest every couple hundred feet.
sentences.zh: 此时的他虚弱到每走几百英尺就不得不坐下来休息。

sentences.en: Eventually, he disappeared into the woods, in the direction of one of his caves.
sentences.zh: 最终，他消失在树林里，朝着他其中一个洞穴的方向走去。

sentences.en: Some days later, on March 24th, a carpenter took his wife to see something interesting, a rock shelter on a local farm.
sentences.zh: 几天后的3月24日，一名木匠带妻子去看一件有趣的东西：当地农场的一个岩洞避难所。

sentences.en: Inside, face down, they found the old Leatherman.
sentences.zh: 在里面，他们面朝下发现了老皮鞋人。

sentences.en: His coat was off.
sentences.zh: 他的外套脱掉了。

sentences.en: He was only wearing one boot.
sentences.zh: 他只穿着一只靴子。

sentences.en: They thought at first he was sleeping.
sentences.zh: 起初他们以为他在睡觉。

sentences.en: He was dead.
sentences.zh: 他已经去世了。

sentences.en: In Ossining, the old Leatherman's body was put into a pine box and buried in an unmarked grave in a cemetery outside town.
sentences.zh: 在奥西宁，老皮鞋人的遗体被放入一口松木棺材中，安葬在镇外墓地的一个无名墓穴里。

sentences.en: His famous suit, meanwhile, went on to live a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他那套著名的衣服却开启了它自己的“传奇人生”。

sentences.en: It was made to sit upright in a chair And displayed in the window of a cigar shop downtown
sentences.zh: 它被做成端坐在椅子上的姿势，并展示在市中心一家雪茄店的橱窗里

sentences.en: Crowds came to stand in the street and stare
sentences.zh: 人群来到街上驻足凝望

sentences.en: Eventually it traveled to New York City
sentences.zh: 最终它被带到了纽约市

sentences.en: Where it was displayed in at least two different museums
sentences.zh: 在那里它至少在两个不同的博物馆里展出过

sentences.en: Around his loop, in the days after his death
sentences.zh: 在他去世后的几天里，在他巡回路线的沿途

sentences.en: People searched the old leatherman's caves And dug holes in the woods
sentences.zh: 人们搜寻了老皮鞋人的洞穴，并在树林里挖了洞

sentences.en: Inspired by rumors of buried treasure
sentences.zh: 在埋藏宝藏的传言鼓动下

sentences.en: No one reported finding any
sentences.zh: 没有人报告说找到了什么

sentences.en: The old leather man left behind a leather backpack, a leather pouch, one leather glove, some homemade pipes, a few simple tools, and according to the coroner,
sentences.zh: 老皮鞋人留下了：一个皮背包、一个皮小包、一只皮手套、一些自制烟斗、几件简单的工具，据验尸官说，

sentences.en: two books made of brown paper and full of figures and hieroglyphics, which could not be deciphered.
sentences.zh: 还有两本用棕色纸做成的、写满数字和象形文字的本子，无法破译。

sentences.en: No one knows what these were, journals or maps, and they don't seem to have survived.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道这些是什么，是日记还是地图，而且它们似乎并没有保存下来。

sentences.en: His suit, people think, was most likely destroyed in a fire on Coney Island.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，他的衣服最有可能是在科尼岛的一场大火中烧毁了。

sentences.en: When the old leatherman died, the answers to his mystery died with him.
sentences.zh: 当老皮鞋人去世时，他身上的谜团也随之烟消云散。

sentences.en: The world moved on.
sentences.zh: 世界向前发展。

sentences.en: Years later, someone stuck a metal pipe in the grass to mark what they thought was the spot of his grave.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，有人在草地上插了一根金属管，来标记他们认为是他墓地的地方。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, that pipe was replaced with a formal headstone, identifying him falsely as Jules Bourglet.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代，那根管子被一块正式的墓碑取代，但上面错误地将他标识为儒勒·布尔莱（Jules Bourglet）。

sentences.en: At the ceremony, a young American girl, dressed in period costume, stood next to a French flag.
sentences.zh: 在仪式上，一个身穿古装的美国小女孩站在一面法国国旗下。

sentences.en: In 2011, the old Leatherman was finally given a proper memorial, the stone with the plaque, where I started my loop.
sentences.zh: 2011年，老皮鞋人终于获得了一座像样的纪念碑，也就是那块带铭牌的石头，那也是我开始徒步的地方。

sentences.en: During this process, the gravesite was moved deeper into the cemetery, away from the road, which gave archaeologists one more crack at the mystery.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，墓地向墓园深处迁移了，远离了道路，这给考古学家提供了又一次破解谜团的机会。

sentences.en: The plan was to exhume the old Leatherman's body and perform DNA analysis.
sentences.zh: 计划是掘出老皮鞋人的遗体并进行DNA分析。

sentences.en: A plan that went on despite community protests, including a website called Leave the Leatherman Alone.
sentences.zh: 尽管遭到社区的抗议，这项计划还是继续进行了，其中包括一个名为“放过皮鞋人”的网站。

sentences.en: In the end, the protest wasn't necessary, because the archaeologists found the perfect thing.
sentences.zh: 最后，抗议其实没有必要，因为考古学家找到了完美的东西。

sentences.en: The old Leatherman was gone.
sentences.zh: 老皮鞋人已经不在了。

sentences.en: It's possible that he and his coffin had already decomposed.
sentences.zh: 可能是他和他的棺材已经分解了，

sentences.en: or that because the grave was originally unmarked, the headstone had been put in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 也可能是因为墓地最初没有标记，墓碑被放错了地方。

sentences.en: Thematically, it's tempting to think that his body is still there, somewhere, just eternally out of reach, that he's even maybe buried under the road.
sentences.zh: 从主题上讲，人们很容易这样想：他的遗体仍然在某个地方，只是永远无法触及，甚至可能就埋在路面底下。

sentences.en: Someone once asked me what I would say to the old leather man if I could meet him.
sentences.zh: 曾经有人问我，如果能见到老皮鞋人，我会对他说些什么。

sentences.en: I thought about it for a minute.
sentences.zh: 我想了一会儿。

sentences.en: Nothing, I said.
sentences.zh: 什么也不说，我说。

sentences.en: That still feels like the right answer.
sentences.zh: 现在看来，这仍然是正确的答案。

sentences.en: I would just stand there with him, silently, in alienated communion.
sentences.zh: 我只会静静地和他站在一起，在一种疏离的共鸣中。

sentences.en: That's what I felt whenever I sat inside one of the old Leatherman's caves.
sentences.zh: 每当我坐在老皮鞋人的某个洞穴里时，我都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I was an intruder, but also at home.
sentences.zh: 我是一个不速之客，却又像回到了家中。

sentences.en: My body was filling the same pocket of rock that he once filled.
sentences.zh: 我的身体正在填满他曾经占据过的那方岩石凹陷。

sentences.en: And the very fact that I was there meant that the old Leatherman was not.
sentences.zh: 而我身处那里的事实，本身就意味着老皮鞋人已经不在了。

sentences.en: My presence guaranteed his absence.
sentences.zh: 我的出现印证了他的缺席。

sentences.en: I was like a hermit crab moving into another crab's shell.
sentences.zh: 我就像一只搬进另一只寄居蟹壳里的寄居蟹。

sentences.en: But it also seemed like he was still there, faintly, just vibrating on a different frequency.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得他仿佛依然还在，隐隐约约地，只是在不同的频率上震动。

sentences.en: Like we were sitting in each other's laps across a distance of 150 years.
sentences.zh: 就像我们跨越150年的时光，坐在彼此的腿上。

sentences.en: We were alone, together.
sentences.zh: 我们孤身一人，却又相伴左右。

sentences.en: Sort of like two patches of leather woven into different parts of the same suit.
sentences.zh: 有点像同一套衣服上织进不同部位的两块皮革。

sentences.en: This paradox is one of the things that fascinates me moSt.
sentences.zh: 这种矛盾是我最着迷的地方之一。

sentences.en: about the old Leatherman.
sentences.zh: 关于老皮鞋人的事。

sentences.en: It is the black hole, you could say, at the center of his loop.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，他是盘旋在他巡回路线中心的黑洞。

sentences.en: He removed himself from society, obviously and dramatically.
sentences.zh: 显而易见又极其戏剧性地，他把自己从社会中剥离了出来。

sentences.en: In doing so, he opted out of all the normal things.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，他选择退出了所有正常的生活。

sentences.en: He never gossiped, never ate in a restaurant, never mailed a letter, never blew out birthday candles.
sentences.zh: 他从不八卦，从不在餐厅吃饭，从不寄信，也从不吹生日蜡烛。

sentences.en: But he also never fully left.
sentences.zh: 但他从未真正彻底离开。

sentences.en: He didn't become a true hermit and disappear forever into the deep woods.
sentences.zh: 他没有成为一个真正的隐士，永远消失在深山老林里。

sentences.en: Day after day, the old leather man put himself right in the middle of all the things he refused to engage in.
sentences.zh: 日复一日，老皮鞋人将自己置身于他所拒绝融入的一切事物正中央。

sentences.en: He walked main roads, passed by schools and shops and town halls.
sentences.zh: 他走过主要道路，经过学校、商店和镇政厅。

sentences.en: And so he remained this bizarre in-between thing, an ever-present absence, a visible invisibility, a speck of isolation injected into the heart of society.
sentences.zh: 因此，他成了一个诡异的中间存在：一个时刻在场的缺席者，一个可见的隐形人，一颗被注射进社会心脏的孤立微尘。

sentences.en: I felt this paradox most strongly in one of the earliest caves I visited, in the town of Bedford Hills, New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约贝德福德希尔斯镇参观最早的几个洞穴之一时，对这种矛盾感触最深。

sentences.en: The cave sits directly behind a combination gas station-Dunkin Donuts, near the intersection of two major traffic arteries,
sentences.zh: 这个洞穴就在一个加油站兼唐恩都乐甜甜圈店的正后方，靠近两条主要交通干道的交汇处，

sentences.en: Interstate 684 and the Sawmill River Parkway.
sentences.zh: 即684号州际公路和锯木河公园大道。

sentences.en: If you know where to look, you can see its opening from the parking lot, a gash of black halfway up the hill.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道往哪里看，从停车场就能看到它的入口，那是在半山腰上的一道黑色裂口。

sentences.en: To get to it, you have to look like a weirdo for about 10 seconds.
sentences.zh: 要想走到那去，你得有大约10秒钟表现得像个怪人。

sentences.en: Walk past the parked cars, hop on top of a retaining wall, and squeeze between some decorative shrubs.
sentences.zh: 走过停放的汽车，跳上一堵挡土墙，然后在一丛装饰性灌木之间挤过去。

sentences.en: But then you are all alone.
sentences.zh: 但随后你就完全孤身一人了。

sentences.en: You have entered the old Leatherman's world.
sentences.zh: 你已经进入了老皮鞋人的世界。

sentences.en: No one will see you fighting your way up the steep slope, which is covered in dead leaves and thorny vines and rotting logs,
sentences.zh: 没有人会看到你艰难地往陡峭的山坡上爬，那里长满了枯叶、带刺的藤蔓和腐烂的木头，

sentences.en: and which is so steep that I lost my footing multiple times and once actually fell and skidded down so hard that my pants filled up with dirt and I lost my cell phone.
sentences.zh: 而且坡度太陡了，我好几次都差点滑倒，甚至有一次真的摔倒并往下滑了好大一段，裤子里塞满了泥土，手机也弄丢了。

sentences.en: I found it later perfectly wedged into the crook of a tree.
sentences.zh: 后来我发现它正好卡在树桠的拐弯处。

sentences.en: The cave, after all that struggle, felt like a refuge.
sentences.zh: 经历了这一切挣扎之后，那个洞穴感觉就像是一个避难所。

sentences.en: Its inside was cool and damp.
sentences.zh: 里面阴凉潮湿。

sentences.en: Crickets lived on the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 天花板上生活着蟋蟀。

sentences.en: Although it was deep enough to disappear into, with a slight right turn at the back, I found myself drawn most powerfully to its opening,
sentences.zh: 尽管它深得足以让人隐入其中——在往后走稍稍向右拐之后——但我发现自己最受吸引的还是它的入口，

sentences.en: that switch point between worlds where the light stops and the darkness begins.
sentences.zh: 那个光明停止、黑暗开始的世界交汇点。

sentences.en: I sat on a rock at the mouth of the cave and looked at the world outside.
sentences.zh: 我坐在洞口的岩石上，看着外面的世界。

sentences.en: Commuters were streaming by at high speeds north and south.
sentences.zh: 通勤者们正以极快的速度向南北方向川流不息。

sentences.en: Down below, the gas station looked like a theater set.
sentences.zh: 在下方，加油站看起来就像一个戏剧布景。

sentences.en: I watched people coming and going, performing the mundane little dramas of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 我看着人们来来往往，上演着日常生活那些平淡无奇的小剧目。

sentences.en: A man walked out double-fisting coffee cups.
sentences.zh: 一个男人手里各拿一个咖啡杯走了出来。

sentences.en: A woman in exercise gear walked her dog.
sentences.zh: 一个穿着运动装备的女人在遛狗。

sentences.en: I saw a fender bender, and I watched the drivers argue.
sentences.zh: 我看到了一起轻微的剐蹭事故，并看着司机们争吵。

sentences.en: Eventually, a policeman came.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，警察来了。

sentences.en: His arms were covered with tattoos.
sentences.zh: 他的胳膊上满是纹身。

sentences.en: The driver of a beige station wagon methodically squeegeed his windshield.
sentences.zh: 一辆米色旅行车的司机一丝不苟地用刮水器刮着挡风玻璃。

sentences.en: It started raining lightly, and people hurried into the store, looking for shelter.
sentences.zh: 天开始下起小雨，人们匆忙跑进店里躲雨。

sentences.en: From the cave, I watched for well over an hour.
sentences.zh: 我从洞里看了足足一个多小时。

sentences.en: And what struck me was, no one had any idea I was there.
sentences.zh: 让我触动的是，根本没有人知道我在那儿。

sentences.en: No one ever looked up.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人抬头看过。

sentences.en: Why would they?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么会呢？

sentences.en: I might as well have been sitting in the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我当时就跟坐在19世纪中期一样。

sentences.en: I was gone.
sentences.zh: 我消失了。

sentences.en: Finally, as the sun slid down the sky, I slid back down the hill.
sentences.zh: 最终，随着太阳在天空中滑落，我也滑下了山坡。

sentences.en: And covered with dirt, with rocks in my pockets, I walked off.
sentences.zh: 我浑身是泥，口袋里装着石头，就这样走了开去。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 随着选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党便陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时甚至令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持自身影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.zh: 《地铁》。
